chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥassān; and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Salamah ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and another, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥassān, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAṭiyyah, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, who raised it to Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام), said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) said: Indeed, Allah has a river beneath His Throne, and beneath the river that is beneath His Throne is a light which He illuminated; and indeed, on the two banks of the river are two created spirits: Rūḥ al-Qudus and a spirit from His command. And indeed, Allah has ten clays: five from Paradise and five from the earth; then he explained the gardens and he explained the earth.

Then he said: There is no Prophet nor Angel after that whom He formed except that He breathed into him from one of the two spirits, and He made the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) from one of the two clays.

I said to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal (عليه السلام): What is al-jabl? He said: The creation other than us, the Ahl al-Bayt; for indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created us from the ten clays and breathed into us from both spirits together, so how excellent its fragrance is.

And another narrated from Abū al-Ṣāmit, who said: The clay of the gardens is Jannat ʿAdn, Jannat al-Maʾwā, Jannat al-Naʿīm, al-Firdaws, and al-Khuld; and the clay of the earth is Makkah, al-Madīnah, al-Kūfah, Bayt al-Maqdis, and al-Ḥāʾir.

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the Household, distinguished in the hadith by their special mode of creation.
key_terms.الْجِنَانِ: The gardens of Paradise whose five divisions are later specified.
key_terms.الْحَائِرُ: Al-Ḥāʾir, listed among the earthly locations corresponding to the clay of the earth.
key_terms.رُوحٌ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ: A spirit from His command, the second created spirit in the report.
key_terms.رُوحُ الْقُدُسِ: The Holy Spirit, one of the two created spirits mentioned in the narration.
key_terms.طِينَاتٍ: Primordial clays or substances of creation, divided into five from Paradise and five from the earth.
key_terms.عَرْشِهِ: His Throne; the exalted divine Throne mentioned as the location above the river.
key_terms.نُورًا: A light beneath the river, presented as part of the primordial cosmological order.

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the creation of Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام), the Prophets, and the Angels?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a cosmological account of creation involving a river beneath the Throne, a divine light, two created spirits, and ten primordial clays from Paradise and the earth. It distinguishes the creation of Prophets and Angels from the unique creation of Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام), who are described as having been created from all ten clays and infused with both spirits together.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Ali Bin Hassan and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Salma Bin Al Khattab, and someone else, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Ali Bin Atiyya, from Ali Bin Raib, 
raising it to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For Allah<sup>azwj</sup> there is a river below His<sup>azwj</sup> Throne, and below the river which is below His<sup>azwj</sup> Throne is a Light of His<sup>azwj</sup> Light, and in the two banks of the river are two created spirits – the Holy Spirit and a Spirit of His<sup>azwj</sup> Command; and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has (therein) ten clays, five from the Paradise and five from the earth’. So he<sup>asws</sup> explained the gardens and explained the earth.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is none from a Prophet<sup>as</sup> nor an Angel kneaded from after it except that in his is one of the two spirits, and Made the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> to be from one of the two clays’. 
I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> the 1<sup style="font-weight: normal">st</sup>, ‘What is the kneading?’

So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘The creation of others than us<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> the People<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> of the Household, for Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Created us from the ten clays and Blew the Spirit into us from both the spirits together. Thus, He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Aromatised the aroma with it’.

And others reported from Abu Al-Samit that he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘The clay of the Gardens is the Garden of Everlasting Bliss, and the Garden of Shelter, and Al-Firdow, and Al-Khuld, and the clay of the earth is Makkah, and Al-Medina, and Al-Kufa, and Bayt Al-Maqdis, and Al-Ha’ir’ (area around the Holy grave of Imam Hussain<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>).
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Ali ibn Hassa’n and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Salma ibn al-Khattab and others from Ali ibn Hassa’n from Ali ibn ‘Atiyya from Ali ibn Ri’ab who has narrated it in a marfu‘ manner from Amir al-Mu’minin (a.s.) who has said the following.

“Allah has a canal below His Throne. Below the canal that is below His Throne is a light that has lighted it up. On both rims of the canal there are two created spirits. One is the holy Spirit and the other is the Spirit from His command. Allah has ten (kinds) of clay. Five from paradise and five from earth.” He then explained the earth and the Paradise.
Then he said, “There is no prophet or angel that He has formed (Jabala) but that He has blown into them from one of those spirits. He has formed the Prophet (s.a) from one of those clays.”

The narrator has said, “I asked abu al-Hassan the 1st , “What is Jabala?” He said, “It is the creatures exclusive of us Ahl al-Bayt (family of Prophet Muhammad). Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most gracious, has created us from ten clays and has into us from both the Spirits and has added fragrance to fragrance.”
